name: Eval, or eyeball?
note: When AI produces output at volume — code across a repo, or generations as a feature — reading samples is the happy-path trap at scale. Pick the approach that actually verifies it.

items.prompt: AI generated 200 product descriptions. You have time to check 10. Best approach?
candidates: Build a small golden set of properties (no banned claims, correct attributes, length bounds) and run all 200 through an automated check; spend your 10 reads on the ones it flags — eval scales, spot-reading doesn't
Read 10 at random; if they're good, ship all 200
Read all 200 — it's the only safe way
Ship all 200; the AI is reliable enough at this volume
items.correct: Build a small golden set of properties (no banned claims, correct attributes, length bounds) and run all 200 through an automated check; spend your 10 reads on the ones it flags — eval scales, spot-reading doesn't
items.explanation: At volume you need an automated standard. Random spot-reading is the happy-path trap (you'll miss the rare bad one), and reading all of it doesn't scale.
items.principle: At volume, build a gate you can run on everything, not a sample you can read.

items.prompt: An agent wrote code across 14 files. What's the scaled version of 'verify against the gate'?
candidates: A test suite encoding your invariants that runs over the whole change in CI, plus property checks for what unit tests miss — the preregistered standard becomes a standing, automated gate
Manually run the happy path in each of the 14 files
Trust the agent's own claim that it tested the code
Ship it and watch production for errors
items.correct: A test suite encoding your invariants that runs over the whole change in CI, plus property checks for what unit tests miss — the preregistered standard becomes a standing, automated gate
items.explanation: At scale the gate is an automated test/eval suite (CI) — preregistration grown up. Manual happy-path runs and self-reported testing don't cover a multi-file change.
items.principle: At scale, the gate is an automated suite — preregistration becomes CI.

items.prompt: Your AI feature generates support answers that vary per run. How do you verify quality?
candidates: Evaluate properties over a sampled set — groundedness, correctness, format — with metrics or an LLM judge against a labeled eval set, not exact-match; non-deterministic output needs measured quality (the discipline from Guide #1)
Assert the output equals a fixed expected string
Check it once; if it's good, it's good
Rely on user complaints to surface the bad answers
items.correct: Evaluate properties over a sampled set — groundedness, correctness, format — with metrics or an LLM judge against a labeled eval set, not exact-match; non-deterministic output needs measured quality (the discipline from Guide #1)
items.explanation: Generative output requires property/quality evaluation (a judge or metrics) over samples. Exact-match fails, single checks don't generalize, and complaint-driven detection lags badly. This is where working-with-AI becomes LLM evaluation.
items.principle: Non-deterministic output is verified by measured quality over samples, not exact match.
